leftEvidence.title: Noah’s water is carried into a baptism statement

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Christ suffers once, is made alive in the Spirit, and the passage moves through imprisoned spirits, Noah, ark, and flood.
points.right: The letter recalls former folly and hostility, then says God’s kindness appeared and salvation came by mercy rather than righteous works.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Baptism is called a corresponding figure and bounded as an appeal of a good conscience through Jesus’ resurrection, not bodily washing.
points.right: Washing of regeneration, renewal by the Holy Spirit, justification, and hope are joined.

payload.posture: Peter explicitly names baptism while Titus names washing and renewal by the Spirit.

rightEvidence.title: Washing and renewal are attributed to divine mercy

payload.tension: Titus never names baptism, and Peter explicitly denies that bodily washing defines the saving claim.
payload.title: Baptism, washing, and the Spirit
